newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela still willing to send troops to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Mandela still willing to send troops to Zaire.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela said on Sunday that after consulting world leaders including U.S. President Bill Clinton he was still determined to contribute South African troops to a multinational force for Zaire.
Mandela told reporters in the Northern Cape provincial capital of Kimberley that a unit could be ready within days.

"We have made a clear statement that we will be involved in the formation of this peace force...We are busy with the matter, but a great deal of discussion is required before we can make any deployment of our troops in the area," he said.
Deputy President Thabo Mbeki on Sunday told a news conference in Rome that countries expected to contribute to the operation would meet in Germany on Wednesday.

He said South Africa had agreed with other African countries that the terms of the multinational mission authorised by the United Nations needed to be changed as a result of the mass refugee migration from Zaire to their homes in Rwanda.

Mandela said he had discussed the matter with Clinton by telephone on Saturday and had also been in touch with French President Jacques Chirac, Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien and United Nations Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali.
